description: Multi-agent system simulating a professional investment board. Specialized AI agents collaborate to ingest market data, analyze investments, and produce structured research reports.

definition_of_done: Repo installable from a fresh clone: pip install -e . with pinned dependencies, no venv/ pip-list instructions
LICENSE file and financial-disclaimer section in README (educational/research use, not investment advice)
pytest suite runs green in GitHub Actions CI without any API keys (Anthropic client mocked, network calls stubbed)
README with architecture diagram, a committed sample report, and a copy-paste quickstart verified on a clean machine
Graceful failure for every missing prerequisite: absent API key, empty vector store, rate-limited data provider

weekly_schedule.weeks_6_7: Step 14 — backtesting engine (stretch; cut without slipping launch)
weekly_schedule.week_8: Buffer: fresh-clone dry run, launch checklist, publish

implementation_steps.title: Core Framework
implementation_steps.description: Build BaseAgent with Anthropic SDK tool-use loop, @tool decorator with auto-schema generation, message types (AgentMessage, AgentResult), and orchestrator skeleton.
key_concepts: Anthropic messages.create() with tools parameter
Tool-use loop: check stop_reason, execute tool calls, feed results back
Pydantic models for typed message passing
@tool decorator generates input_schema from Python type annotations

implementation_steps.title: Data Layer
implementation_steps.description: Define abstract data provider interfaces, implement Yahoo Finance provider, build SQLite cache, define Pydantic data models (Quote, OHLCV, etc.).
key_concepts: Abstract base classes for swappable data providers
yfinance library for free market data
SQLite cache with TTL to respect rate limits
Pydantic models for data validation

implementation_steps.title: Market Data Agent
implementation_steps.description: First working agent end-to-end. Implement market data tools (get_stock_price, get_historical_ohlcv, get_market_indices), wire them into a MarketDataAgent that inherits BaseAgent, write the system prompt.
key_concepts: Agent inherits BaseAgent and registers its tools
System prompt defines the agent's role and output format
Test by running the agent with a simple task like 'Get me AAPL price data'

implementation_steps.title: RAG System
implementation_steps.description: Set up ChromaDB vector store, implement sentence-transformers embeddings, build document chunking (section-aware for SEC filings), create SEC EDGAR provider using edgartools, build ingestion pipeline, implement Research Analyst agent with search_knowledge_base tool.
key_concepts: ChromaDB for persistent vector storage with metadata filtering
Section-aware chunking splits 10-K/10-Q on Item sections
edgartools library for SEC EDGAR access (free, no API key)
RAG retrieval tool filters by ticker, filing_type, date

implementation_steps.title: Remaining Agents
implementation_steps.description: Build Alternative Data agent (FRED + insider txns), Quant Analyst (returns, correlations, regression), and Risk Manager (VaR, Sharpe, drawdown, basic Black-Scholes). Stub backtesting and stress testing.
key_concepts: fredapi for FRED economic data
scipy.stats for statistical calculations
Historical VaR and parametric VaR
Black-Scholes option pricing with scipy

implementation_steps.title: Committee Chair & Orchestration
implementation_steps.description: Build the Committee Chair agent that uses delegate_to_agent as a tool to call other agents. The Chair receives a hypothesis, decides which agents to consult, synthesizes their outputs. Wire up the CommitteeOrchestrator to manage a full session.
key_concepts: delegate_to_agent tool instantiates and runs sub-agents
Chair's system prompt defines the decision framework (Thesis/Evidence/Risk/Recommendation)
Context accumulation: each agent result feeds into the Chair's conversation
No hard-coded pipeline — Claude decides the execution order

implementation_steps.title: Report Generation
implementation_steps.description: Build Jinja2-based report generator that takes agent outputs and produces formatted markdown investment memos. Create templates for investment memo, risk report, and committee decision.
key_concepts: Jinja2 templates with markdown output
Structured sections: Thesis, Market Data, Fundamentals, Risk, Recommendation
Include data citations and source attribution

implementation_steps.title: CLI & End-to-End Pipeline
implementation_steps.description: Build the CLI entry point, wire up the full pipeline (hypothesis → orchestrator → agents → report), finalize all configuration files, create .env.example and .gitignore, test end-to-end.
key_concepts: argparse or click for CLI
InvestmentHypothesis Pydantic model for input validation
Full pipeline test: 'Evaluate NVDA as a long position'
Output: data/reports/nvda_analysis.md

architecture_notes.orchestration_pattern: Committee Chair is an agent that uses delegate_to_agent as a tool. Claude's reasoning decides which agents to call and in what order — no hard-coded pipeline.
architecture_notes.data_abstraction: Abstract provider interfaces (MarketDataProvider, etc.) allow swapping free APIs for premium without changing agent code.
architecture_notes.agent_tool_loop: BaseAgent runs: send messages → if stop_reason=='end_turn' return → else execute tool calls → append results → repeat.
architecture_notes.rag_strategy: Section-aware chunking for SEC filings, ChromaDB with metadata filtering (ticker, filing_type, date), sentence-transformers for free local embeddings.
architecture_notes.scaling_path: Phase 2 (pre-launch): cache integration, packaging/tests/CI, robustness, docs — then backtesting as stretch. Phase 3 (post-launch): signal generation, portfolio construction, streaming data feeds.

phase1_deliverable.command: python scripts/run_committee.py --ticker NVDA --hypothesis "Evaluate NVDA as a long position given AI infrastructure demand growth" --output data/reports/nvda_analysis.md
phase1_deliverable.output: Multi-section investment memo with market data analysis, fundamental research from SEC filings, basic risk metrics, economic context, and a synthesized Buy/Sell/Hold recommendation with conviction level.

phase2_steps.title: Async Parallel Agents
phase2_steps.description: Convert BaseAgent to async, run sub-agents in parallel using asyncio.gather when they have no dependencies. Significantly reduces end-to-end latency.
key_concepts: async/await with Anthropic async client
asyncio.gather for parallel agent execution
Dependency graph: which agents can run concurrently
Async tool execution

phase2_steps.title: Cache Integration
phase2_steps.description: Wire the existing SQLite cache into all data providers. Cache API responses with configurable TTL to reduce latency and respect rate limits.
key_concepts: Decorator-based caching for provider methods
Configurable TTL per data type (quotes shorter, filings longer)
Cache invalidation strategies

phase2_steps.title: Packaging, Test Suite & CI
phase2_steps.description: Create pyproject.toml with pinned dependencies (it was listed in steps 2 and 8 but never actually created — the project currently has no dependency manifest at all). Add MIT LICENSE. Migrate the eight root-level test_*.py scripts into a tests/ pytest suite that runs offline by mocking the Anthropic client and stubbing provider network calls. Wire up GitHub Actions running ruff + pytest on every push.
key_concepts: pip install -e . must work from a fresh clone — replaces the README's manual pip-install list
unittest.mock / pytest fixtures to fake messages.create() responses including tool_use blocks
Recorded fixture data for yfinance/FRED/EDGAR so CI never hits live APIs
CI green badge in README

phase2_steps.title: Robustness & First-Run Experience
phase2_steps.description: A public user's first run must not end in a stack trace. Validate API keys at startup with actionable error messages, handle provider rate limits and network failures with retry/backoff, degrade gracefully when the vector store is empty (Research Analyst should say so, not crash), and add per-run cost estimation/ceiling so strangers don't get surprise API bills.
key_concepts: Fail fast at startup: check ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / FRED_API_KEY before spending tokens
tenacity-style retry with exponential backoff on 429/5xx from data providers
Empty-knowledge-base fallback path for search_knowledge_base
Token/cost budget per committee session, printed at end of run

phase2_steps.title: Docs, Sample Reports & Demo
phase2_steps.description: Rewrite README for a public audience: quickstart verified on a clean machine, architecture diagram (Mermaid), committed example reports so visitors see the output without an API key, terminal demo GIF, and a prominent disclaimer that this is an educational/research tool and not investment advice.
key_concepts: Financial disclaimer is non-negotiable for a public tool producing Buy/Sell/Hold output
Committed sample memo (e.g. examples/nvda_analysis.md) is the highest-leverage marketing asset
Mermaid diagram of Chair → sub-agent delegation flow
Document expected per-run API cost so users aren't surprised

phase2_steps.title: Backtesting Engine (stretch)
phase2_steps.priority: stretch — cut before slipping the launch date
phase2_steps.description: Complete the stubbed backtesting engine as the one pre-launch feature differentiator: test simple entry/exit strategies against historical data, integrated as a Quant Analyst tool. Only start after steps 10–13 are done; weeks 6–7 of the schedule with week 8 held as buffer.
key_concepts: Strategy definition (entry/exit rules)
Historical simulation with transaction costs
Performance metrics: total return, max drawdown, win rate
Avoid look-ahead bias

phase3_post_launch.title: Signal Generation
phase3_post_launch.description: Automated signal generation based on technical indicators and agent outputs. Trigger alerts when conditions are met (e.g. RSI below 30, unusual volume).
phase3_post_launch.deferred_reason: Multi-week feature that does not block a public release; adds ongoing-monitoring scope beyond the core research-report deliverable.

phase3_post_launch.title: Portfolio Construction
phase3_post_launch.description: Portfolio Manager agent with mean-variance optimization, risk parity, position sizing, and concentration constraints.
phase3_post_launch.deferred_reason: Changes the product from single-ticker research to portfolio management — a scope expansion, not launch polish.

phase3_post_launch.title: Streaming Data & Live Monitoring
phase3_post_launch.description: Real-time data feeds and a monitoring pipeline that re-evaluates positions when market conditions change.
phase3_post_launch.deferred_reason: Requires always-on infrastructure and paid data feeds; incompatible with the free-tier, run-on-demand design being launched.

phase3_post_launch.title: Finish stubbed agent capabilities
phase3_post_launch.description: Sentiment/shipping data for Alternative Data agent; stress testing for Risk Manager (both stubbed in Phase 1).
phase3_post_launch.deferred_reason: Partial agents are honest and documented; completing them is incremental depth, not launch-blocking.
